full_judgment: 9. In his evidence as DW 1 defendant No.1 Dr Nairnur Rahman states that they got the property of schedule 'A' from their father by a deed of gift in 1957 and he made some improvement in the property at a cost of Taka 71,000.00 out of his personal fund before making a gift of his 50% share in the property in favour of his wife, defendant No. 2, on 1-12-70. He further states that his wife spent Taka 74,000.00 from her own fund for making improvement in the property of schedule 'A'. DW 1 further states that he applied to the DIT in 1960 for allotment of a plot at Gulshan and the DIT allotd the plot in the name of the defendant in 1960 and he paid Taka 24,750.00 as premium out of his own fund and completed construction of a residential house for his own benefit and interest and he let it out to the Embassy of Switzerland by executing a deed of lease (Ext. R) dated 24-11-73. DW 1 asserts that there was no oral agreement between him and his brother within the knowledge of their relations about sharing of the two houses. Rema Tea Company and Shahabazpur Tea Company arc not their joint business and these are private limited Companies in which there are other share-holders. Pubali Jute Mills was not their joint business and it is a private limited company nationalised in the year 1972 and again handed over after denationalisation in the year 1973. In his evidence DW 1 clearly mentions that for the property of Schedule 'B', the application for allotment of a plot at Gulshan, the letter of allotment and delivery of possession and all other papers are exclusively in his name and he claims sole ownership of this property. In cross-examination DW 1 mentions that his father had six tea companies in Jalpaiguri and he migrated to former East Pakistan in 1947, purchased Shahabazpur Tea Company in 1950 and Rema Tea Company in 1951 with the sale proceeds of the property in India. His father died on 4-7 -69. He had several houses in India and he sold the same in 1947-48.
